question: A 59-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis is brought to the physician by his wife for a 1-week history of progressive abdominal distension and yellowing of the eyes. For the past month, he has been irritable, had difficulty falling asleep, become clumsy, and fallen frequently. Two months ago he underwent banding for esophageal varices after an episode of vomiting blood. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows jaundice, multiple bruises, pedal edema, gynecomastia, loss of pubic hair, and small, firm testes. There are multiple small vascular lesions on his chest and neck that blanch with pressure. His hands are erythematous and warm; there is a flexion contracture of his left 4th finger. A flapping tremor is seen on extending the forearms and wrist. Abdominal examination shows dilated veins over the anterior abdominal wall, the spleen tip is palpated 4 cm below the left costal margin, and there is shifting dullness on percussion. Which of the following physical examination findings are caused by the same underlying pathophysiology?

options.ope: Multiple bruises and loss of pubic hair

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> decreased liver function -> impaired metabolism -> 80% CHAIN: Impaired liver function -> decreased production of clotting factors -> easy bruising -> 85% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> portal hypertension -> dilated veins -> 70% CHAIN: Portal hypertension -> splenomegaly -> palpable spleen tip -> 75% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> decreased metabolism of estrogen -> gynecomastia -> 80% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> decreased metabolism of estrogen -> palmar erythema -> 75% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> shunting of blood -> caput medusae -> 70% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> shunting of blood -> spider angiomata -> 75% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> decreased metabolism of sex hormones -> testicular atrophy -> 80% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> decreased albumin production -> abdominal fluid accumulation -> abdominal distension -> 85% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> decreased metabolism of sex hormones -> loss of pubic hair -> 75% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> impaired detoxification -> elevated bilirubin -> jaundice -> 90% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> impaired detoxification -> elevated bilirubin -> yellowing of the eyes -> 85% CHAIN: Liver cirrhosis -> impaired detoxification -> elevated ammonia -> flapping tremor -> 80%
analysis: The physical examination findings that are caused by the same underlying pathophysiology in this patient are palmar erythema and gynecomastia. These findings are both associated with chronic liver disease, specifically alcoholic cirrhosis.
